"Speedmaster" series The "Speedmaster" was born in 1957 as a model with a highly visible dial and high operability. In 1965, NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) selected a wristwatch that could withstand use in outer space. The "Speedmaster" was the only one that passed the test with various watches from each company. In addition, the "Speedmaster" selected by the National Aeronautics and Space Administration was used in the Apollo program and in 1969 won the honor of being the first wristwatch to land on the moon. In 1970, when Apollo 13 encountered a major accident in which an oxygen tank exploded on its way to the moon, we gained further trust by controlling the rocket injection time and making it possible for everyone to return safely. Since its birth, various models have been announced, and even now, it is a series that maintains reliability as an official equipment of NASA (National Aeronautics and Space Administration) and continues to keep accurate time.
